ai.title: Include original values in agent tool validation errors
ai.summary: Malformed tool call errors from set-output and spawn-agent-utils now append the original input value. This helps debugging by showing exactly what was passed before truncation. The change is limited to agent-runtime error handling.

eli5.text: When the assistant generates output that doesn't match the expected format, or when someone asks it to start another assistant with a bad prompt or settings, the error message now includes the exact text that caused the problem (cut off if it's very long, with a note that it was shortened). This means you'll see what the assistant tried to submit instead of just a generic 'something went wrong' alert, making it easier to figure out what needs fixing.

ai.title: Refine base2 agent prompts for type casting and file writing
ai.summary: Updated base2 agent system prompts to clarify type casting exceptions and prefer str_replace over write_file for targeted edits. Also adjusted free-tier agent spawning instructions to include separate typecheck tasks for local changes and the whole project. These tweaks aim to improve code quality and efficiency based on recent eval misses.

eli5.text: If you use the free version of this tool to edit files, you'll now get two separate type checks during reviews: one for your recent edits and one for the entire project. This helps catch both small mistakes and bigger issues that might break other parts of your codebase. The change also slightly relaxes a coding rule, allowing type casting exceptions when a value can genuinely accept any type.

ai.title: Bash agent spawn params requirement
ai.summary: Updated basher spawnerPrompt to mandate explicit command params. Prevents validation failures caused by prompt-only spawns. Applies to agents/basher.ts.

eli5.text: The assistant now refuses to run unless you give it a specific command to execute. Before this change, it could be started with just a description of what output you wanted, which sometimes caused it to fail. Now, every request must include the exact shell command, so the assistant won't try to run without knowing precisely what to do.

ai.title: Enable writetodos for free mode
ai.summary: write_todos tool is now enabled for free mode in agents/base2/base2.ts. Previously gated by !isFree, it is now only gated by !isFast. System prompt instructions for using write_todos on 3+ step tasks now include isFree in the condition.

eli5.text: If you are on the free plan and ask the agent to work through a multi-step problem, it will now write out a step-by-step plan for you to follow along. Previously, only paid plans got that plan-writing helper; the agent would skip it for free users. Now, whether you are on a free or paid account, the agent will break down longer tasks into a checklist it shows you before diving in, so you can see exactly what it intends to do and in what order. The change only affects how the agent organizes its work, not the quality or depth of the work itself.

System prompt refactored to instruct spawning `code-searcher` agent for refactoring awareness and context gathering. `code-searcher` agent prompt updated to enforce `searchQueries` parameter format with examples.

eli5.text: When the base2 agent needs to find existing code to understand what it's changing, it now spawns a dedicated code-searcher agent instead of using a built-in search tool. This means refactoring tasks that involve updating multiple references to a function or variable will use a more specialized search approach, potentially finding more accurate matches across the codebase. If you watched this in action, you'd see it spin up a separate search-focused agent rather than performing searches inline, and the search agent now requires queries in a specific structured format with examples provided.

ai.title: Spawn gemini thinker for complex problems only
ai.summary: The `thinker-with-files-gemini` agent is now spawned only for complex problems, skipping routine edits and clearly-scoped changes. This reduces unnecessary agent overhead while maintaining quality for difficult tasks. The agent's reasoning effort was bumped from 'low' to 'medium' to improve its performance on these complex queries. This change affects the free tier agent orchestration logic in `agents/base2/base2.ts` and the agent definition in `agents/thinker/thinker-with-files-gemini.ts`.

eli5.text: If you're on the free plan and need help with something tricky, the system now saves a particularly smart assistant for the hardest questions instead of sending it for every small edit. That smart assistant also thinks a bit harder when it does show up, so it can work through tougher problems more carefully. You'd notice it only getting pulled in for the bigger, less straightforward tasks, while quick or clearly defined edits are handled faster without the extra overhead.

ai.title: Centralize tool error value formatting
ai.summary: Extracted inline JSON stringification and truncation logic into formatValueForError in packages/agent-runtime/src/util/format-value.ts. Updated tool-executor.ts, set-output.ts, and spawn-agent-utils.ts to use the new helper, which adds type annotations for primitive values. Scope limited to agent-runtime tool error surfaces.

eli5.text: When the assistant's tools run into a problem, it shows you the original input that caused the error, but it now formats and truncates that input in a single, consistent way. Previously, each tool that displayed error details (like tool execution, output validation, and agent spawning) had its own slightly different logic for converting the input to text and cutting it off, which could lead to inconsistent or messy error messages. The change pulls that repeated code into one shared helper, so every error message now shows the original values cleanly, adds type information for simple values like numbers or true/false, and caps the length consistently at 500 characters before truncating. You'll notice cleaner, more predictable error messages with the original input when something goes wrong

ai.title: Basher agent input schema simplification
ai.summary: Basher agent schema in agents/basher.ts replaces top-level prompt and rawOutput with optional what_to_summarize param. LLM summarization now triggers only when what_to_summarize is provided; absent field returns raw output. Spawner prompt updated to reflect new contract. Affects core agent definitions only.

eli5.text: When you run a command in the terminal, the system now only uses extra smart analysis to explain the output if you specifically ask it to focus on something. If you don’t specify what you want explained, you just get the raw result without any summary. This makes the process simpler and avoids unnecessary processing.

ai.title: Add optional schema for subagent params
ai.summary: Replaces generic record with structured Zod schema for subagent params in spawn-agents.ts. Defines optional fields for command, searchQueries, filePaths, and url to guide model tool calls. Scope limited to common/src/tools/params/tool/spawn-agents.ts. Schema uses .catchall(z.any()) to allow unlisted parameters while enforcing known field types.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to spin up a helper for you, say, a code search or a terminal task, it can now hand that helper a clearly labeled set of hints, like which search terms to look for or which files to read, instead of passing a freeform bag of values. The assistant can still add extra details beyond the known hints, so it doesn't lose flexibility, but the most common inputs are now described in plain language so the helper knows what you expect. If you watched a helper being started, you'd see it receive tidier, better-labeled instructions rather than a shapeless list of parameters.

ai.title: CLI release 1.0.640 with 100k read limit and free-mode writetodos
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.640 in `cli/release/package.json`, shipping the accumulated CLI and agent-definition changes. The `read-files` tool now truncates to 100,000 characters (replacing the 1,000-char cap by removing `TRUNCATE_TO_CHARS` in favor of `MAX_CHARS`). The `write_todos` tool is enabled in free mode, dropping the `!isFree` gate so it is only blocked by `!isFast`. The base2 agent replaces the in-process `code_search` tool with a spawned `code-searcher` agent, the Basher agent adopts a simplified `what_to_summarize` param schema, and the `thinker-with-files-gemini` agent runs only on complex problems with reasoning bumped to medium. Affected surfaces span the CLI package manifest, `agents/base2/base2.ts`, `agents/basher.ts`, and `sdk/src/tools/read-files.ts`.
ai.evidence: The diff `cli/release/package.json` shows a one-line version increment from `1.0.639` to `1.0.640`. The analysis notes list multiple user-visible changes (read-files truncation to 100k, writetodos enabled in free mode, base2 prompt refinements, Basher schema simplification, code-searcher spawn replacement, and gemini thinker scoped to complex problems) accompanying this version bump.

eli5.text: This release gives free users the ability to write and track task lists during work, lets agents read much larger files (up to 100,000 characters), and improves how agent tools validate and report errors. The write-todos feature is now enabled for free mode, so you can break projects into checkable steps without paying. File reading now covers far bigger source files, with clear guidance on what got trimmed if a file is too long. Agent tool calls that fail now include the original input that caused the failure, making debugging faster. The Basher agent now requires explicit commands in its parameters, preventing misfires, and its summary behavior is cleaner. Subagent parameters use a proper schema, so the agent knows what inputs are expected for each helper.

ai.title: Freebuff version bumped to 0.0.31
ai.summary: Release version for the freebuff CLI package advanced from 0.0.30 to 0.0.31 via an update to the version field in freebuff/cli/release/package.json. This version bump packages the day's accumulated agent-runtime and agent-definition work, including the 100k-character read-files truncation limit, Basher command parameter clarifications, centralized tool error value formatting, the code-searcher agent spawn substitution, and the gemini thinker complex-problem gating. No functional code changes accompany the bump itself; it is a pure packaging increment over the prior commit sequence.
ai.evidence: Modified file freebuff/cli/release/package.json: version field in the freebuff package bumped from 0.0.30 to 0.0.31 (commit 14679103, release-bump nature).

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.31 ships with smarter, more capable AI agents that work better on complex coding tasks. The main highlights: (1) You can now read much larger files at once - the tool handles up to 100,000 characters instead of just 1,000 before cutting off; (2) The system is more careful about which AI helper it sends your work to, only sending tricky problems to the most advanced model and using a lighter touch for simple edits; (3) Error messages now show exactly what input caused problems, so when something goes wrong you'll see what value triggered it; (4) Agents can now write to-do lists and search codebases more effectively, making multi-step projects easier to track and navigate. Upgrading gives you better troubleshooting, fewer wasted steps on simple tasks, and more reliable results when tackling harder problems - all while getting clearer feedback when something needs your attention.

ai.title: Update buffbench single eval agent and task IDs
ai.summary: Agent ID changed from base2 to base2-free-evals and task ID from filter-system-history to server-agent-validation in evals/buffbench/main-single-eval.ts. This aligns the single eval configuration with the free eval agent suite. Scope limited to internal evaluation harness. No user-facing surface or model picker changes.

eli5.text: The internal test that rates how well our assistant performs has been retuned to measure the assistant against a different set of benchmarks. Specifically, the test now evaluates a variant called "base2-free-evals" on a task named "server-agent-validation" instead of the previous "base2" agent and "filter-system-history" task. This only affects the behind-the-scenes scoring system used by developers; nothing you see or interact with has changed.

ai.title: GLM-5.1 added to free agents and model picker
ai.summary: GLM-5.1 (`z-ai/glm-5.1`) replaces Minimax-M2.5 as the default model for `base2-free`, `editor-lite`, and `code-reviewer-lite` agents. The update includes new Fireworks pricing configs, deployment mappings, and type definitions for the new model. `MAX_AGENT_STEPS_DEFAULT` increases from 100 to 200 in `common/src/constants/agents.ts`, affecting CLI run configs.

eli5.text: The free version of the assistant can now use a newer, more capable model instead of the previous one. If you use the free editor, code reviewer, or base helper tools, you'll get responses from a different AI without doing anything, it just happened automatically. The system also lets these free tools run for longer before stopping, so complex tasks have more room to complete. This change is already live for free users.

ai.title: Freebuff version bumped to 0.0.32
ai.summary: The freebuff CLI package version advanced from 0.0.31 to 0.0.32 in freebuff/cli/release/package.json, packaging a day of agent-runtime and agent-definition work. This release ships GLM-5.1 as the new default free model for base2-free, editor-lite, and code-reviewer-lite agents, replacing Minimax-M2.5, alongside a raised MAX_AGENT_STEPS_DEFAULT from 100 to 200 in common/src/constants/agents.ts. It also restores the 100,000-character truncation limit on read-files (removing the previous 1,000-char cap), enables write_todos in free mode, swaps the base2 agent's in-process code_search tool for a spawned code-searcher agent, and gates the gemini thinker agent on complex problems with reasoning bumped to medium. The CLI release at cli/release/package.json now carries version 1.0.640 with these accumulated CLI and agent-definition changes.
ai.evidence: Commit f8cd385f changes the single line "version" from 0.0.31 to 0.0.32 in freebuff/cli/release/package.json, a pure packaging increment bundling the day's accumulated changes.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.32 drops in a new default AI model and lets key agents run longer before stopping. The smarter GLM-5.1 model now powers the base2-free, editor-lite, and code-reviewer-lite agents, replacing the older Minimax-M2.5 and bringing updated pricing and support. The step limit for these agents doubled from 100 to 200, so complex coding tasks can keep going instead of cutting off early. The evaluation harness also got tidier labels for tracking agent performance, which means more reliable accuracy checks behind the scenes. Upgrading gives you faster, more capable code help that can tackle bigger tasks before restarting.

If you were watching the configuration list, you would see that helper's custom entry turned into a comment on the line, while the other helpers remain unchanged. This is already live today.

ai.title: Escape on askuser form interrupts assistant stream
ai.summary: Added `onInterruptStream` prop to `ChatInputBar` and wired it in `Chat`. The `handleFormSkip` function now calls `onInterruptStream()` immediately after `skip()`. This ensures the assistant stream is properly interrupted when the user escapes the `ask_user` form. Files changed: `cli/src/chat.tsx`, `cli/src/components/chat-input-bar.tsx`.

eli5.text: When you press Escape while the assistant asks you a question in a pop-up form, the assistant now fully stops talking instead of continuing in the background. Previously, the assistant's response kept streaming even after you dismissed the form, so you had to wait for it to finish before starting over. Now, dismissing the form cleanly interrupts the assistant and lets you begin fresh immediately.

ai.title: Update Fireworks routing test fixtures
ai.summary: Test fixtures in `web/src/llm-api/__tests__/fireworks-deployment.test.ts` switch from `minimax-m2p5` to `glm-5p1`. The `STANDARD_MODEL_ID`, `DEPLOYMENT_MODEL_ID`, and `originalModel` arguments in `createFireworksRequestWithFallback` calls now reference `z-ai/glm-5.1`. This aligns test expectations with current model routing logic.

eli5.text: The internal test harness for the assistant's model routing switch from one underlying model (minimax-m2p5) to another (z-ai/glm-5.1), updating both the test data and expected routing identifiers to match the current model configuration. Only developers running the verification suite observe any difference. The switch is already live in production systems, so the routing tests merely realign internal expectations with the live model selection.

ai.title: Context Pruner agent model switched to claude-sonnet-4.6
ai.summary: The `context-pruner` agent definition now specifies `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6` as its model, replacing `openai/gpt-5-mini`. This change updates the model used for summarizing and condensing conversation context when limits are exceeded. The modification is contained within `agents/context-pruner.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant that keeps your conversations from running out of space now listens to a different brain, it quietly switched from the previous thinking engine to a newer one from a different provider. You will not see settings to change this yourself, but when your chat gets long and the system summarizes what happened so far, the summary is produced by the new engine. That behind-the-scenes swap is already live today.

ai.title: Include tools in token count API for accurate billing
ai.summary: Token counting logic now accepts and processes tool definitions, specifically converting them to Anthropic format for precise input token calculation. The `callTokenCountAPI` and `postTokenCount` endpoints were updated to pass `tools` in the payload, while `run-agent-step.ts` maps internal tool definitions to the expected schema. This change ensures that token usage is accurately reflected when tools are present, primarily affecting Anthropic models, with a 30% buffer applied for non-Anthropic providers like OpenAI and Gemini to account for tokenizer differences. Files modified include `packages/agent-runtime/src/llm-api/codebuff-web-api.ts`, `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts`, and `web/src/app/api/v1/token-count/_post.ts`.

eli5.text: The token counter that determines your bill now includes the tools (functions) the assistant uses, so you're charged for the full size of your tool definitions, not just the message text. When you use OpenAI or Gemini models, an extra 30% is automatically added to the count because those systems count tokens slightly differently than Anthropic's method. If you looked at a billing estimate while using tools, you'd see the number tick up to reflect the actual size of the tool descriptions and parameters being processed.
